item.title: Truck carrying ammonia crashes in Russellville, nearby businesses evacuated
item.description: A truck carrying anhydrous ammonia rolled over in Russellville on Wednesday, resulting in nearby businesses being forced to evacuate.

item.title: CARTI holds ribbon installation for ‘Day of Hope’
item.description: The Central Arkansas Radiation Therapy Institute held its 3rd annual “Day of Hope” on Wednesday.

item.title: Arkansas represented at the nation’s largest Black History Month parade
item.description: The largest Black History parade, the 38th Annual African American History Parade Celebration, is taking place this Saturday in Shreveport, Louisiana, and Arkansas is being represented.

item.title: Morrilton food truck raises money for families who lost their children in Monday night house fire
item.description: Three children were killed in a house fire in Conway County Monday night – and now, the community of Morrilton is stepping up to help the families involved.

item.title: Maumelle’s newest park pays homage to their former Department of Public Safety building
item.description: The City of Maumelle started construction on its Millwood Station, which would pay homage to the former Department of Public Safety building that used to stand in the same space.

item.title: Vilonia teen faces long recovery after sledding accident in Cabot
item.description: What began as a fun snow day quickly turned into a life-altering ordeal for a Vilonia family after their 16-year-old daughter was seriously injured in a sledding accident in Cabot.

item.title: 'It's catastrophic.' White Hall's only grocery store to be demolished following winter storm damage
item.description: For over four decades, the current Brookshire's location has served as White Hall's only grocery store. Now, residents will have to go out of town to shop after the building was condemned following damage from last weekend's winter storm.

item.title: Arkansas police raise safety concerns over potentially dangerous social media trend
item.description: Following an uptick in a social media trend prank, Fayetteville residents are speaking out about their concerns for the neighborhood.

item.title: Little Rock Christian Academy star JJ Andrews talks McDonald's All American game, future with the Razorbacks | Full Court(ney) Press
item.description: Sports Director Courtney Mims sat down with 5-star Razorback commit JJ Andrews to talk about getting picked for the McDonald's All-American game, coming back from a recent injury and what his goals are for improving his game with the Hogs.

item.title: Lawsuit accuses North Little Rock pastor of sexually abusing teen
item.description: A lawsuit accuses a pastor at a North Little Rock church of sexually abusing a teen girl.
